assessment: Assignment changes and renames correlate with affected exports; their causal roles remain unproven. Replacement delays exceed execution time. The clean privacy sample excludes a course split, and coordinator checking versus importing effort is unmeasured.

openings.claim: Move course-scope reconstruction into a private, center-and-week-specific export manifest. A coordinator confirms intended course identities once; the exporter uses that manifest rather than reconstructing scope from current instructor assignments. Assignment changes and renames become signals to recheck the affected manifest before generating the documented CSV.
openings.delta: Hybrid parents: explicit scope manifests and change-triggered reconciliation. Their interaction converts disruptive changes into targeted review prompts. The speculative capability is automatic reconstruction of course identity and lineage for any week; it depends on stable identifiers, effective-dated assignment/name/split history, and center ownership checks. A presently testable partial capability uses manually confirmed staging manifests plus scripted change comparisons, with secure regeneration from the confirmed scope.
openings.prediction: If repeated scope reconstruction drives the excess work, manifest-based exports should reduce missing-course corrections and active checking time on changed-assignment and renamed-course tasks; unchanged-course tasks should gain less.
openings.probe: Within six engineer-days and existing hosting, compare incumbent and manifest workflows in two short, counterbalanced sessions with each consenting coordinator, using fabricated participants and changed, renamed, unchanged, and split-course scenarios. Measure confirmation, checking, download, correction, and import time separately; inspect course completeness, CSV compatibility, center isolation, and concurrent attendance entry. Include initial manifest preparation in handling time. Only a subsequent 40-export run can establish the stated operational target.
assumptions: Coordinators can establish intended scope despite conflicting or stale timetables; confirmation does not establish truth by itself.
Failure boundary: absent history, ambiguous splits, or unreliable identities require explicit reconciliation rather than automatic inclusion.
Manifest storage and regeneration can fit existing private infrastructure without blocking attendance entry; this requires verification before deployment.
Participant data stays in the private service and authorized center workspace; manifests supplement the existing CSV schema.
